papers.title: Beyond Bot Labels: Retrospective Consequence-Grounded Ranking of Attributed Cache Harm in E-Commerce Logs
papers.abstract: Web caches reduce origin load and latency, but automated traffic can either warm them or evict objects shoppers reuse, lowering the cache hit ratio (CHR). Existing bot defenses generally infer automation from User-Agent (UA) strings or behavior rather than identify sessions that impose cross-session cache harm. We instead formulate the task as ranking sessions by eviction damage and propose consequence-grounded session ranking. A single chronological replay attributes each eviction-induced miss by a protected shopping session (a victim) to the session whose insertion last evicted the object. A behavioral model predicts the target from session behavior alone. Selected sessions bypass the cache but remain origin-served. In a controlled check of 539 non-victim sessions selected across harm levels, attribution order tracks victim-hit changes after removal (Spearman correlation 0.80). On a 12.7-million-request real trace, the top 1% of sessions carry 48.8% of attributed harm. Sessions without bot tags contribute 49.1% of this tier's harm. At the 20% request-volume target, the default conditional CHR difference reaches 93% of the UA baseline, which selects 47 times as many sessions. Six training seeds show little variation. This comparison conditions on the victims that remain, so we also report victim bypass. Local replay and retraining on a second store reproduce harm concentration and a top tier dominated by sessions without bot tags. These results establish attributed cross-session harm as an outcome-based target for retrospective cache audits and selective intervention design.

papers.title: uhd-rfsoc: Bringing Off-the-Shelf RFSoC Boards to Unmodified UHD Applications
papers.abstract: Next-generation wireless research relies on software-defined radios (SDRs) with more channels and larger bandwidth. The USRP family is one of the most widely used SDR platforms, and much of the wireless software ecosystem is built on top of the USRP hardware driver (UHD). However, each USRP model comes with a fixed channel count, bandwidth, and streaming capability. Off-the-shelf radio frequency system-on-chip (RFSoC) boards, on the other hand, integrate up to 16 analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) and 16 digital-to-analog converters (DACs) operating at several gigasamples per second (GS/s), but existing UHD applications cannot directly use them. We present uhd-rfsoc, an open-source FPGA design and host software stack that turns these boards, including the 16-channel ZCU216 and the RFSoC 4x2, into standard UHD devices without modifying UHD. Through standard UHD calls, applications can configure the carrier frequency, channel count, the per-channel I/Q sample rate, and the wire format. uhd-rfsoc combines timestamped, flow-controlled sample transport in the FPGA with data plane development kit (DPDK) packet processing and vectorized sample conversion on x86 and Arm hosts. The built bitstreams for a number of RFSoC board configurations with varying RF data converter rates, channel counts, I/Q sample rates, and wire formats all successfully pass UHD's built-in streaming benchmarks. We further demonstrate compatibility with unmodified GNU Radio flowgraphs, a custom GPU-accelerated transceiver digital signal processing pipeline, as well as the OCUDU and Duranta 5G radio access network stacks using both software and commodity user equipment.

papers.title: PUMA-Former: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Computation Offloading in MEO-LEO Satellite Networks With Incomplete Information
papers.abstract: Satellite edge computing distributes mobile workloads across moving processors whose service capacity must be coordinated over time. In medium Earth orbit (MEO)--low Earth orbit (LEO) networks, periodic reports leave CPU states stale or missing, making offloading sensitive to uncertain capacity and shared-destination congestion. We propose PUMA-Former, an uncertainty-aware agentic framework for cooperative offloading under incomplete information that balances completed work, service delay, and execution cost. A MEO coordinator maintains distinct-report memory and closes the loop between available evidence, capacity estimates, allocation commands, and execution feedback. Latent-delay attention weights plausible measurement-age hypotheses, and historical innovations refine CPU estimates around the latest received report. Queue-error-aware fusion incorporates auxiliary pressure while accounting for backlog uncertainty. The inferred resource moments condition a structured Transformer allocator for joint destination, partition, bandwidth, CPU, and power decisions. Bounded risk-aware calibration then adjusts workload splits to reflect uncertainty and shared destination load. In traffic-driven development evaluation, PUMA-Former increases admitted compute-work completion by 8.62%, reduces mean modeled service delay by 34.78%, and reduces mean episode-P95 delay by 71.08% relative to ATLA-adapt. It also improves completion and normalized energy over fixed-half round-robin offloading. Service gains over the learning baselines involve higher normalized energy.

papers.title: INC-SRv6: In-Network Route Exploration and Fast Failover Using Segment Routing Headers in Dynamic UAV Networks
papers.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks require a network provisioning mechanism that guarantees delivery and latency quality of service (QoS) under dynamic conditions in next-generation airborne mesh networks by continuously learning and repairing multi-hop paths under rapid link turnover without flooding the control plane. This paper presents INC-SRv6, an in-network computing routing mechanism that repurposes the IPv6 Segment Routing Header (SRH) and its Segments Left (SL) pointer into a self-learning, fast-failover distributed control plane. Rather than treating the SRH as a static source-committed vector, INC-SRv6 uses the active SL pointer to partition the segment list in flight: slots ahead of SL provide capacity for hop-by-hop next-hop recording, while the suffix behind SL serves as an in-band multi-destination reachability vector. Through this dual-zone header discipline, transit routers extract distance-weighted reachability updates from arriving suffixes, gate admission by single-pass confidence with bounded binary probing, advance or reverse SL deterministically, and restore pre-transmission SRH state for local failover upon link loss. Simulations across 200-node 3D UAV networks show that under high-speed flight and repeated 20% relay outages, INC-SRv6 improves packet delivery over reactive routing (92.12% versus 89.12%) while cutting 95th-percentile tail delay from 121.26 to 8.84 ms and control packets by 35.8%, with a 4-byte compact uSID stride model reducing SRv6 control bytes by over 52%.

papers.title: Mobile Edge Deployment and Resource Management for Maritime Wireless Networks
papers.abstract: Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) has been envisioned as one of the key technologies for supplying computation and storage resources in Internet of Vessels (IoV) networks. Due to its flexible deployment, low cost and agile maneuverability, Unmanned Surface Vehicle (USV) has emerged as a promising solution, to provide communication and computation services for maritime users. In this paper, we study mobile edge deployment and resource management for MEC-assisted maritime wireless networks where USVs with diverse computation resources are deployed to provide edge computing services that complement the cloud-based services. To this end, we formulate an optimization problem to minimize the expected response time by jointly optimizing the deployment of mobile USVs and computation offloading decisions. To solve the mixed-integer nonlinear program problem, we propose a Dual-Layer Reinforcement Learning (DLRL) framework to attain a near-optimal solution. Specifically, a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm is designed to obtain the best USV deployment in the outer layer learning, and a Q-learning algorithm is designed to determine the best computation offloading decisions in the inner layer learning. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed solution outperforms some literature algorithms by effectively handling both continuous and discrete variables.

papers.title: Resource Management and Trajectory Optimization for UAV-IRS Assisted Maritime Edge Computing Networks
papers.abstract: With the exponential growth of maritime wireless devices and the rapid development of maritime applications, traditional maritime communication networks encounter communication and computation limitations in supporting computation-intensive and latency-critical tasks. Edge computing and Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) have emerged as promising techniques to improve communication and computation services for maritime devices with limited computation capabilities and battery capacity. This paper studies an IRS Mounted on Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UIRS) assisted maritime edge computing network, in which the UIRS is deployed to assist the transmission from Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) to the edge server via Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) protocol. We propose a resource management and trajectory optimization scheme by jointly optimizing subslot duration, offloading ratios, transmit power, edge computation capability allocation, UIRS phase shifts and UIRS trajectory, aiming at minimizing the overall energy consumption. Since the non-convex nature of the optimization problem, we propose a two-layered method by decomposing the original problem into two subproblems. The top-layered subproblem is solved by the Semi-Definite Relaxation (SDR) method and the underlying-layered subproblem is solved by the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm. Numerical results demonstrate that our proposed scheme can effectively and efficiently reduce overall energy consumption.

papers.title: Quantum Shock and Train-Time Constrained Quantization: A Geometric Study of Finite-Resolution Variational Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: Finite-resolution interfaces map Variational-Circuit angle to discrete codebook. Since Pauli rotations are periodic, so Euclidean rounding may produce wrong codeword near a chart boundary; error due to coordinates alone cannot measure how much the final state was changed. Herein we define a metric, Quantum Shock, for Pure State it is defined as the average of the square of the Fubini-Study distance (over all inputs) between the pre-deployment and deployed states. This value is limited by constant multipliers of the mean of infidelity and provides upper limits on displacement when observing bounded quantities and margin based predictive stability. Extensions to the analytical Bures-angle for mixed-states were derived, along with a finite shot stability bound. The proposed Train-Time Constrained Quantization allows a delay in applying a penalty for selecting a codeword aligned with periodicity until after task only optimizations. Three small binary tasks were evaluated on a four qubit, two layer classifier using ten matched seeds, K = 4, 8, 16 and exact expectation values from simulation under noiseless conditions and state vector simulations. On our primary evaluation, T-CQ exhibited smaller average local quantum shock compared to circular post-training quantization for each task and code-book size tested. The re-execution on the x86-64 platform using K=8 preserved the direction of the mean-shock comparison but had varying magnitudes.

papers.title: Space-based Zero-trust Architecture for Securing the Direct-to-Cell Paradigm
papers.abstract: The rapid evolution of Direct-to-Cell (D2C) technology has emerged as a pivotal enabler for ubiquitous 6G global coverage, seamlessly connecting massive numbers of User Equipment (UEs) in remote and underserved areas. However, by bypassing traditional terrestrial satellite access gateways, the D2C paradigm inadvertently renders conventional front-end security perimeters obsolete. Consequently, malicious UEs can directly expose satellites and their core networks to severe security vulnerabilities. To address these critical threats, this article proposes a Space-based Zero-Trust Architecture (SZTA) empowered by on-board satellite computing. Specifically, the proposed SZTA consists of three core components: radio frequency (RF) fingerprint-based authentication, distributed identity management, and behavior-driven dynamic access control. This architecture enables continuous, real-time verification of UE identity authenticity and behavioral legitimacy, effectively mitigating the inherent network-layer security risks of D2C networks. Simulation results demonstrate the robustness, effectiveness, and efficiency of the proposed SZTA. Finally, to facilitate the practical deployment of {the SZTA}, we discuss key technical challenges, propose corresponding solutions, and outline open research issues to guide future investigations.

papers.title: Starlight: Whittle-Driven Fidelity Rescue for Satellite-Terrestrial Quantum Networks
papers.abstract: A planetary-scale quantum internet is constrained by exponential attenuation in terrestrial fibers. Low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites provide a low-loss vacuum backbone, but limited satellite resources must be allocated among competing connections under continuously evolving and heterogeneous physical conditions. Existing satellite scheduling remains largely provisioning-oriented, optimizing satellite-resource assignment for aggregate entanglement delivery. Recent age-based approaches instead incorporate chronological freshness into entanglement scheduling. Neither line of work directly identifies the connections most urgently requiring satellite assistance as their physical states evolve. We propose Starlight, a demand-driven satellite-terrestrial entanglement routing architecture that targets degrading connections before their terrestrial entanglement becomes unusable. Starlight introduces Effective Age of State (EAoS), a physics-aware metric that maps heterogeneous decoherence and swapping-induced fidelity penalties onto a unified additive coordinate. Representing each connection by evolving EAoS, we formulate rescue scheduling as a Restless Multi-Armed Bandit (RMAB) problem and derive a closed-form Whittle-style index approximation for top-K selection. Starlight further employs a two-timescale control plane and an asynchronous dispatch-and-mask pipeline to suppress redundant in-flight allocations. Simulations show that Starlight achieves up to 84.5% average satisfaction under constrained rescue capacity and sub-0.5-ms orchestration at 1,000 connections, while remaining robust to heterogeneous memory decay and stochastic atmospheric degradation.

papers.title: Evaluating Polling Schemes for OFDMA Uplink Scheduling in Time-Sensitive Wi-Fi Networks
papers.abstract: IEEE 802.11ax introduced orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA) to improve channel utilization through concurrent multi-user transmissions. For effective uplink (UL) scheduling, the access point (AP) requires timely knowledge of buffered traffic at the stations (STAs). Explicit buffer-status polling provides this, yet each polling round can query only as many STAs as there are resource units (RUs). Scheduled-access, random-access, activity-based, and learning-based schemes address this buffer-status acquisition problem differently and have generally been evaluated in isolation under different conditions, so it remains unclear how they compare across time-sensitive workloads. We evaluate common schemes from the Wi-Fi standard and literature under three time-sensitive environments: a large-scale teleconferencing session, an industrial IoT deployment, and an extended reality (XR) service. The relative performance of the schemes depends strongly on traffic characteristics and offered load. In conferencing, activity-based and learning-based polling perform best, while conventional contention-based access remains competitive under light load. In the industrial scenario, scheduled-access most effectively delivers time-sensitive packets within their deadlines under heavy load, whereas contention-based access performs best under lighter load. In XR, OFDMA-based schemes achieve high video throughput that contention-based access cannot sustain; among them, activity-based polling achieves the lowest deadline-miss ratios for uplink head-tracking traffic, at the expense of longer video delay tails. These findings highlight the importance of selecting channel access and scheduling schemes according to traffic requirements and operating conditions.

papers.title: Wireless Node Ranking via Fourier-Driven Maximum-Likelihood Estimation (extended version)
papers.abstract: We apply non-abelian Fourier theory to the problem of maximum-likelihood estimation of the order of a line topology, based on signal strength measurements under shadowing only. This yields up to a 60-fold speedup over standard methods for uncorrelated shadowing. Moreover, for correlated Gaussian shadowing with a singular covariance (e.g. the joint path-loss model), maximum-likelihood recovery is exact and independent of the shadowing variance (an infinite Le Cam threshold), which our implementation confirms for $\sigma/\alpha$ as high as 7.0. The key object is the covariance's null space. Its dimension is fixed by the topology; its orientation depends on the correlation function only through the per-link variances. Although the mechanism formally requires an exact line, it is robust to small perturbations of the formation: an approximate kernel recovers as well as the exact one. We explore the dependence on the perturbation in detail for five nodes.

papers.title: PRISM: A Post-Prediction Reliability Framework for Evidence-Guided Correction and Selective Abstention
papers.abstract: A model may produce a prediction with high confidence and still get the outcome wrong. This is a challenge in sequential applications, where the system evolves over time and deployment data may differ from the data used during training. To address this issue, we propose PRISM (Prediction Reliability and Intelligent Self-Correction Mechanism), a framework that evaluates prediction reliability after the initial output is generated. It estimates the risk of error and examines predictions identified as potentially unreliable. For these cases, PRISM analyses available signals, retrieves similar situations from historical data, and verifies whether an alternative prediction is supported by the evidence. It can then retain the original prediction, apply a verified correction, or abstain when the evidence is insufficient. We evaluate PRISM on second-innings match prediction in the Indian Premier League (IPL). Ball-by-ball records are converted into over-level observations to capture changes in match conditions throughout an innings. To preserve temporal order, earlier IPL seasons are used for training, IPL 2024 for validation, and IPL 2025-2026 for out-of-time testing. The dataset contains 8,665 over-level observations from 475 matches, with the test partition comprising 2,568 observations from 142 matches. In one experimental record, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and HistGradientBoosting achieve accuracies of 65.2%, 68.4%, and 70.2%, respectively. The corresponding PRISM evaluation reports a selective accuracy of 82.4% at 88.5% coverage, with a Brier score of 0.126 and an expected calibration error (ECE) of 0.019.

papers.title: Who sets the consent signal? Platform defaults and crawl coverage in measuring opt-outs from AI training
papers.abstract: Web data used in social research and in the training of AI models increasingly carry consent signals, but who sets these signals is rarely measured. This paper attributes opt-outs from AI training to the party that set them. The complete lists of Polish, Czech, Slovak, Hungarian and German domains recorded by Common Crawl, with 3,445,751 reachable sites, were crawled in October 2026 together with a random sample of 10,000 Slovak registry domains. Each signal was matched against vendor templates and identical files. Four exploratory hypotheses were examined with logistic models. Between 0.70% and 3.82% of the listed sites opt out. Platform and hosting defaults set 15% to 78% of the opt-outs. Settings active by default reach 60% to 95% of a vendor's sites, while settings that owners switch on reach at most 2.1%. Most of the higher Czech and Slovak rates compared with Germany are statistically attributable to platforms. Lists derived from Common Crawl miss about a third of the Slovak opt-outs because they exclude sites that block its crawler. The results describe delegated consent, a signal that a platform sets on behalf of its users, which measurements of consent on the web must consider.

papers.title: A Theory of Information Architecture for Networked Decisions: Freshness, Locality, and Coordination
papers.abstract: A broader view of a network can help agents coordinate, but collecting that view takes time. When is a fresh local observation more useful than an older view of the whole network, and when should an agent look only partway across it? We study agents that repeatedly minimize a shared quadratic cost in an environment that evolves independently of their actions. An information architecture specifies what each agent observes and how old those observations are. Each agent uses a synchronized neighborhood snapshot, so extending its scope also ages the nearby readings used in the decision. We assume that the optimal action with complete information is affine in the state, and that the conditional mean of the current state equals the old state scaled by a common exponential decay factor. Using the classical Marschak--Radner decomposition, we derive the delay threshold beyond which fresh local information outperforms a complete but older global view. This comparison allows non-Gaussian states and nonlinear decision rules. We then determine how far an agent should look by balancing the benefit of additional observations against their greater age. In a Gaussian spatial model on a line, we derive the optimal observation radius: looking beyond the local node pays only when information travels more than twice the spatial correlation length in one coherence time. The preferred information architecture also depends on the decision being made. On a fixed 64-node ring, increasing only the reach of the decision weights from 0.7 to 6 hops shifts the optimal observation radius from one to five hops.

papers.title: Enhancing Quality of Experience in Future Telecommunication Networks: A Review of Frameworks and Machine Learning Algorithms
papers.abstract: Quality of experience (QoE) has emerged as a key measure of user satisfaction for multimedia services, including adaptive video streaming, immersive media (AR/VR) and cloud gaming. As services grow more varied, QoE assessment has to connect measurement with the models that act on it. Existing surveys treat the two as separate catalogues and do not classify how they are coupled, so the choice of an integrated architecture is neither replicable nor transferable. This survey addresses four questions: (1) how frameworks are coupled with ML models, (2) which QoE actions each pattern supports, (3) which patterns appear in each service domain, and (4) which problems remain open. A taxonomy of loose, tight, and distributed/federated coupling answers them, in which each work is coded by where model inference runs. This paper also identifies three enhancement mechanisms (predictive optimization, adaptive resource allocation, content-aware enhancement). Because reported accuracies use different metrics and datasets, they cannot be ranked directly. A model-selection guide is therefore derived from verified results. The study traces three generations, from static measurement through reactive ML to proactive and generative methods, including large language model integration, and examines domain constraints for immersive media, cloud gaming and the Internet of Things. Open challenges include generalizability, interpretability, model drift and privacy, while objective tuning, federated scheduling, multi-modal and mobile-edge integration are emerging directions.

papers.title: Hard/Soft NLoS Detection via Combinatorial Data Augmentation for 6G Positioning
authors: Seung Min Yu (Korea Railroad Research Institute
Jihong Park (Singapore University of Technology and Design
papers.abstract: A key enabler for meeting the stringent requirements of 6G positioning is the ability to exploit site-dependent information governing line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) propagation. However, acquiring such environmental information in real time is challenging in practice. To address this issue, we propose a novel NLoS detection algorithm termed combinatorial data augmentation-guided NLoS detection (CDA-ND), which builds upon our prior work. CDA-ND generates numerous preliminary estimated locations (PELs) by applying multilateration over many gNodeB (gNB) combinations using a single snapshot of range measurements. When a target gNB is in NLoS, the resulting PELs split into two clusters: one derived using the target gNB's range measurement and the other derived without it. Their displacement is summarized by a single vector, called the NLoS evidence vector (NEV), which is used to compute an NLoS likelihood score. Based on this score, two modes of NLoS detection are developed. First, each gNB is classified as LoS or NLoS, termed hard decision (HD), using a simple threshold test. Second, each gNB's NLoS confidence is probabilistically quantified, termed soft decision (SD), which extends HD with weak site-survey priors, namely empirical NLoS-score samples and the average NLoS probability. We then design positioning algorithms tailored to these two modes by excluding gNBs deemed NLoS and re-weighting the remaining gNBs for SD. The proposed CDA-ND achieves high reliability in indoor factory environments under frequency range 1, attaining NLoS detection accuracies of 96.8% and 91.5% when the proportion of NLoS gNBs is approximately 18% and 56%, respectively. As a result, integrating CDA-ND into positioning significantly reduces mean absolute error by about 22% and 67% in LoS- and NLoS-dominant environments, respectively.
